examples.text: Look out of the window [i.e. lean out] while I speak to you.
I have[…]more feet than shoes, or such shoes as my toes look through the overleather.

glosses: To check, to make sure (of something).

examples.text: Finding it was like to overblow, we took in our Sprit-ſail, and ſtood by to hand the Fore-ſail; but making foul Weather, we look'd the Guns were all faſt, and handed the Miſſen.

glosses: To look at; to turn the eyes toward.

examples.text: Serene, smiling, enigmatic, she faced him with no fear whatever showing in her dark eyes.[…]She put back a truant curl from her forehead where it had sought egress to the world, and looked him full in the face now,[…].

glosses: To seek; to search for.

examples.text:
c. 1552–1599, Edmund Spenser, unidentified sonnet,
Looking my love, I go from place to place,
Like a young fawn that late hath lost the hind;
And seek each where, where last I saw her face,
Whose image yet I carry fresh in mind.

glosses: To influence, overawe, or subdue by looks or presence.

examples.text: to look down opposition

A Spirit fit to start into an Empire,
And look the World to Law.
Ovid might have evaded her entreaties by means of an excuse. But her eyes were irresistible: they looked him into submission in an instant.

glosses: To look at a pitch as a batter without swinging at it.

examples.text: The fastball caught him looking.

glosses: Pay attention.

examples.text: Look, I'm going to explain what to do, so you have to listen closely.

examples.text: Let’s have a look under the hood of the car.

examples.text: He gave me a dirty look.

glosses: The visual sense.

examples.text: The car was quite pleasing to the eye, but impractical.

glosses: The iris of the eye, being of a specified colour.

examples.text: Brown, blue, green, hazel eyes.
Natalie’s brown eyes looked into Jim’s blue eyes, and the girl and boy flirted.

glosses: Attention, notice.

examples.text: That dress caught her eye.

In the eyes of Mr. Farquhar Fenelon Cooke the apotheosis of the Celebrity was complete. The people of Asquith were not only willing to attend the house-warming, but had been worked up to the pitch of eagerness. The Celebrity as a matter of course was master of ceremonies.

glosses: The ability to notice what others might miss.

examples.text: He has an eye for talent.

Nothing was too small to receive attention, if a supervising eye could suggest improvements likely to conduce to the common welfare. Mr. Gordon Burnage, for instance, personally visited dust-bins and back premises, accompanied by a sort of village bailiff, going his round like a commanding officer doing billets.

glosses: A meaningful look or stare.

examples.text: She was giving him the eye at the bar.
When the car cut her off, she gave him the eye.

glosses: Ellipsis of private eye.

examples.text: Far more annoying were the letters from parents of missing daughters and the private detectives who had begun showing up at his door. Independently of each other, the Cigrand and Conner families had hired “eyes” to search for their missing daughters.

glosses: A hole at the blunt end of a needle through which thread is passed.
The oval hole of an axehead through which the axehandle is fitted.

examples.text: [H]e struck the Duffer a sharp blow on the back of the head with the eye of the axe, and left him stunned and senseless on the earth[.]

glosses: A fitting consisting of a loop of metal or other material, suitable for receiving a hook or the passage of a cord or line.

A loop forming part of anything, or a hole through anything, to receive a hook, pin, rope, shaft, etc.; for example, at the end of a tie bar in a bridge truss, through a crank, at the end of a rope, or through a millstone.
A burner on a kitchen stove.
The relatively calm and clear centre of a hurricane or other cyclonic storm.
A mark on an animal, such as a butterfly or peacock, resembling a human eye.
The dark spot on a black-eyed pea.
A reproductive bud in a potato.
The dark brown centre of a black-eyed Susan flower.
That which resembles the eye in relative beauty or importance.

examples.text: The “e” was a bit over-inked, with a blacked-out eye.

examples.text: My becomings kill me, when they do not eye well to you.
